items.title: Amazon’s Alexa Tablet 12 Pro ditches Fire OS for real Android
items.excerpt: Amazon killed the Fire tablet name and rebuilt the line as Alexa Tablets with real Android, the full Google Play Store, and Alexa+ built in. The 12 Pro starts at $499.99 with a 120Hz screen, plus a pen and a keyboard case that turn it into a work machine.
items.rationale: A new hardware line: Amazon has replaced Fire tablets with Android-based Alexa Tablets that have Alexa+ built in, priced from $499.99. The 10-10 card was a one-year Alexa+ review, which is a different event.

items.title: I played Android's first AI frame-gen game: Mobile just had its DLSS moment
items.excerpt: Arm and Sumo Digital's Neural Dawn uses Arm's Neural Super Sampling and Denoising plus Neural Frame Rate Upscaling, AI networks running on the Mali G2 Ultra GPU, to bring ray-traced MegaLights to a phone; it currently runs only on MediaTek Dimensity 9600 Pro devices.
items.rationale: The first playable phone game that uses on-GPU AI upscaling and frame generation, with named hardware support (Dimensity 9600 Pro). Games ran Arm's tech explainer on 09-09; this hands-on is a new release.

items.title: Homelabber uses second-gen Optane memory sticks to run a 2.8-trillion-parameter AI model on CPU alone
items.excerpt: A Reddit homelab user ran Moonshot AI’s 2.8-trillion-parameter Kimi K3 CPU-only on Optane PMem 200 at 0.85 tokens/s with a 1-bit quant.
items.rationale: A new local-AI hardware hack: a frontier-size model running on CPU alone with Optane PMem, with a measured speed and a heat warning. The nearest card is the jailbroken-PS5 local-AI hack (10-18), which used different hardware.

items.title: Just 2% of Tom's Guide readers want AI in earbuds & headphones — so why do audio brands keep pushing it on us?
items.excerpt: Results are in: just 2% of Tom's Guide readers buy earbuds and headphones because of AI features. So why do audio brands think we want them?
items.rationale: New reader-survey data (2%) on whether people want AI in audio gear, set against recent AI-earbud launches. It adds a demand-side angle to the section's hardware coverage.

items.title: Underdog shows off a 32MB speech model in new demo
items.excerpt: Underdog released Woof, a 31M-parameter (32MB) open speech-and-music generation model that runs offline on most devices, demoed in a browser game; it follows the 167MB on-device Bark speech-to-text model and a 27B laptop-class model aimed at private, local AI.
items.rationale: A new model release: Woof, an open 32MB speech-and-music generator that runs offline on ordinary devices. It goes beyond Underdog's 10-06 launch and is a different product from Ollama's Mac TTS (10-28).

https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/06/underd.new_action: Underdog released a new model, Woof: a 31M-parameter (32MB) open speech-and-music generation model that runs offline, shown in a new browser-game demo. The 10-06 card covered the company launch, not this release.
